check_plan.behavior: On train_001, produce the required template-compatible dispatch-control JSON for every memo order, with classifications and output formatting validated against the task's live records and public inputs.
check_plan.required_evidence: The public target task and its official evaluation outcome are required; private expected answers are not supplied.

check_plan.behavior: On train_004, preserve the ability to prepare the allocation decision file from its own memo, template, and live ERP records; do not apply TRAIN_EXPEDITE_A-specific output categories where the train_004 template differs.
check_plan.required_evidence: The public regression task and its official evaluation outcome are required; private expected answers are not supplied.

change_intent.expected_behavior: For the observed TRAIN_EXPEDITE_A workflow, read the memo and output template, gather live evidence needed for each memo order, keep inventory/shortage and SKU-exception classifications distinct from customer exceptions, fulfillment decisions, and next actions, then perform a per-field completeness and consistency pass before returning template-compatible JSON sorted by order_id with two-decimal currency. The procedure must not invent task-specific derivation rules when the authoritative records or instructions do not establish them.

alternatives: The mismatches may instead reflect incorrect interpretation of task-specific ERP fields or decision rules that are not visible in the supplied excerpts.
The missing matches may reflect incomplete, incorrect, or stale live-record retrieval, but the provided evidence does not show the complete API request and response sequence.
The final artifact may contain serialization or template-field errors in addition to classification errors; the complete artifact and template are not available in the evidence excerpts.
hypotheses.claim: A reusable procedural checklist that separates per-order evidence collection for inventory/shortage and SKU exceptions from fulfillment decisions and next actions may reduce the observed classification mismatches in the TRAIN_EXPEDITE_A dispatch-control workflow.

necessity.behavior_delta: Add a narrowly scoped procedural capability for the observed Northwind dispatch-control workflow: derive and verify each required category per order independently, rather than treating matched order-set or customer-exception fields as evidence that inventory, SKU exception, decision, and action fields are also correct.
necessity.capability_gap: The supplied base snapshot contains no Skills. No provided capability instructs a structured, field-by-field evidence worksheet and final consistency pass for the required multi-category dispatch-control output.
unknowns: No existing Skill bodies or revisions are present in the supplied snapshot, so no existing capability can be compared for overlap or patched.
The complete memo, answer template, ERP queries and responses, and final artifact are not visible; the evidence does not establish the exact rule or retrieval error behind any failed classification.
This is a local procedural improvement hypothesis for train_001. Repeated utility beyond this workflow is not established, and train_004 is retained only as a regression check.

operation_constraints.atomic_operation_count: Each PATCH edit, ADD, RETIRE and asset edit counts once.
operation_constraints.rule_anchors: Rule IDs refer to the original expected_revision; newly added rules cannot be targeted in this patch.

inputs.evaluation_scope: Local procedural improvement for the observed GDPevo train_001 workflow; train_004 is a regression check. No general transfer claim. The actor can query official read-only business GET endpoints, read public input files and selected Skill assets, and submit an answer. It cannot execute scripts or access grading materials. Only the trusted checks in verification_catalog are supplied in this pilot.

verification_catalog.description:
Check the public task: {"description":"Northwind Components operations has an expedite queue for wave TRAIN_EXPEDITE_A. Use the local queue memo in input/payloads/expedite_queue_memo.json and the shared Northwind ERP API to prepare the dispatch-control answer.

Shared API entry point: `<TASK_ENV_BASE_URL>`

For each order in the memo, classify the inventory status, customer exception, final fulfillment decision, next action, SKU exception lists, and shipping quote. Use the live API records for orders, products, customers, inventory, warehouses, and shipping quotes. Return only JSON matching input/payloads/answer_template.json.

Keep records sorted by order_id. Currency must be rounded to two decimals.

Check the public task: {"description":"Northwind Components needs the allocation desk decision file for order wave TRAIN_TRANSFER_B.

Use the shared ERP API described in the task group environment README. Use the API base URL supplied by the runner as `<TASK_ENV_BASE_URL>`. Inspect the live ERP records for the wave, customers, products, warehouses, and inventory as needed. A short desk memo is available in input/payloads/allocation_memo.md.

Return a single JSON object matching input/payloads/answer_template.json. The decision file should classify every order line in TRAIN_TRANSFER_B as one of the allowed actions, include transfer requests where internal movement can clear the shortage, identify account-blocked orders, and summarize the wave.

value.expected_behavior: For the observed TRAIN_EXPEDITE_A workflow, read the memo and output template, gather live evidence needed for each memo order, keep inventory/shortage and SKU-exception classifications distinct from customer exceptions, fulfillment decisions, and next actions, then perform a per-field completeness and consistency pass before returning template-compatible JSON sorted by order_id with two-decimal currency. The procedure must not invent task-specific derivation rules when the authoritative records or instructions do not establish them.

checks: Run case:train_001 against the public task and official evaluation outcome to validate template-compatible per-order dispatch-control JSON, independent category derivation, order sorting, and two-decimal currency formatting.

Run case:train_004 against the public task and official evaluation outcome to confirm the procedure does not impose TRAIN_EXPEDITE_A dispatch-control categories where the allocation template and memo differ.
exceptions: If authoritative records or instructions do not establish a required derivation, do not fabricate a task-specific rule; use only the template- and instruction-supported representation for unavailable or inapplicable information.
If the task's template or memo defines a different workflow, categories, or action vocabulary, follow that task's own materials rather than importing dispatch-control categories.
preconditions: The task memo and answer template are readable.
Official read-only ERP endpoints are available through the task-supplied base URL.

applies_when: A Northwind task provides a memo or queue, an answer template, and live ERP records and requests per-order dispatch-control classifications, decisions, actions, SKU exceptions, or shipping quotes.
The task instructions and supplied template define the required fields and allowed output structure.
exclusions: Do not apply this procedure's dispatch-control category names or derivation assumptions to allocation/transfer tasks whose memo or template defines different fields or allowed actions.
Do not invent task-specific classification, fulfillment, or shipping rules when they are not established by the task instructions, memo, template, or authoritative live records.
Do not substitute matched customer-exception or order-set results for independent verification of inventory, SKU-exception, decision, action, or quote fields.

steps: Read the task instructions, memo, and answer template first; enumerate every memo order and every required output field without adding fields not present in the template.

For each memo order, retrieve the authoritative live records needed by the requested fields, including order, product/SKU, customer, inventory or warehouse, and shipping-quote records when the task requires them.

Create a per-order evidence worksheet that records separately: inventory or shortage evidence; SKU-specific exception evidence; customer-exception evidence; fulfillment-decision evidence; next-action evidence; and shipping-quote evidence.

Derive each requested classification, decision, action, exception list, and quote only from the applicable task instructions, memo, template, and retrieved records. Keep evidence and conclusions for these categories separate.
Populate the template-compatible JSON only after every memo order has values or task-supported empty values for every required field.

Perform a final per-field consistency pass: confirm every memo order is represented once, records are sorted by order_id, category values agree with their own evidence, the JSON has exactly the template-required structure, and currency values are rounded to two decimals when required.
Return only the completed JSON artifact.
content.title: Verify Northwind Dispatch-Control Fields Independently
triggers: A Northwind expedite or dispatch-control task requires JSON derived from a queue memo, answer template, and live ERP data.

value.reason: The supplied evidence supports a narrowly scoped, reusable procedural addition for the observed TRAIN_EXPEDITE_A workflow: independently collect and verify per-order evidence for inventory/shortage, SKU exceptions, customer exceptions, fulfillment decisions, next actions, and quotes before producing the template JSON. No existing Skills are available to patch. The proposal preserves the required train_004 regression obligation and does not assert unobserved task-specific ERP derivation rules.
